chunks: The Day of Tarwiyah was only named thus because there was no water at Arafat, and they used to draw water from Makkah for their quenching. Some of them would say to others, “Have you provided yourselves with water? Have you provided yourselves with water?” So it was called the Day of Tarwiyah for that reason.

key_terms.الْمَاءِ: Water, which pilgrims carried for their need
key_terms.بِعَرَفَاتٍ: At Arafat, the well-known place connected to the hajj rites
key_terms.تَرَوَّيْتُمْ: Have you taken water for yourselves or quenched yourselves
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah, from where water was brought
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The Day of Tarwiyah, the eighth day of Dhu al-Hijjah in the rites of hajj

ai.seo_question: Why is the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah called the Day of Tarwiyah?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the historical reason for the name of the Day of Tarwiyah during hajj. It states that because there was no water at Arafat, pilgrims would bring water from Makkah and ask one another whether they had taken provision of water, and from this the day received its name.
